structures.name: Segment II
objects: Left posterior lateral segment of liver (II)

rows: Location
Upper part of the left lateral section of the liver, to the left of the falciform ligament.
Features
Like every liver segment it has its own branch of the portal vein, hepatic artery and bile duct, so it can be removed on its own.

structures.name: Segment III
objects: Left anterior lateral segment of liver (III)

rows: Location
Lower part of the left lateral section of the liver, to the left of the falciform ligament.
Features
Like every liver segment it has its own branch of the portal vein, hepatic artery and bile duct, so it can be removed on its own.
Location

Left medial section of the liver, between the falciform ligament and the plane of the middle hepatic vein, which runs from the gallbladder fossa to the inferior vena cava. Its lower part is the quadrate lobe.
Features
Like every liver segment it has its own branch of the portal vein, hepatic artery and bile duct, so it can be removed on its own.
Location
Lower part of the right anterior section of the liver, next to the gallbladder.
Features
Like every liver segment it has its own branch of the portal vein, hepatic artery and bile duct, so it can be removed on its own.
Location
Lower part of the right posterior section of the liver.
Features
Like every liver segment it has its own branch of the portal vein, hepatic artery and bile duct, so it can be removed on its own.
Location
Upper part of the right anterior section of the liver, under the dome of the diaphragm.
Features
Like every liver segment it has its own branch of the portal vein, hepatic artery and bile duct, so it can be removed on its own.
Location
In a fossa on the lower surface of the liver. Its fundus reaches the edge of the liver at the tip of the right 9th costal cartilage.
Function
Stores and concentrates bile and releases it into the duodenum when cholecystokinin makes it contract.
Blood supply
Cystic artery, usually a branch of the right hepatic artery.
hy: In acute cholecystitis, pressing under the right ribs stops the patient from breathing in (Murphy sign), and the pain may be felt in the right shoulder.
